content.text: Community members sought clarification on the ElizaOS ecosystem structure. Stan outlined four distinct components: ElizaOS is the core agent framework, ElizaCloud is the infrastructure hosting layer, Milady is a consumer-facing UI for personal task management, and Waifu is a side project where agents compete and manage their own economies running entirely on ElizaCloud. Odilitime also clarified that Waifu Fun does not have its own token, that Solace on Waifu has a token called Waifu, and that the team has not left ElizaOS despite community speculation to the contrary.

Developer Ben (Smeltor) introduced a multi-chain DeFi abstraction project covering swap, earn, perps, bridge, and borrow functionality across protocols including Kamino, Aave, Morpho, Compound, and Hyperliquid in a single non-custodial integration that returns signable calldata. He asked whether builders prefer an abstraction layer or owning each individual integration. Separately, developer Navneet Sahu announced plans to build a comprehensive Kamino plugin for ElizaOS, noting Kamino is one of the most significant protocols on Solana and has shown interest in AI adoption. Stan confirmed all plugins now live in the elizaOS/eliza repository and advised building on the develop branch with frequent rebasing.

Odilitime clarified that Hyperforge is the world-building component of a project called Hyperia, which is a separate team and not a joint venture. Both Hyperia and ElizaOS were started by Shaw, though Shaw may now serve only as an advisor to Hyperia while focusing primarily on ElizaOS, Milady, Waifu, and cloud initiatives. Ana-Maria from NeverBell, a project building infrastructure for AI agents to interact with financial markets through natural language and controlled execution, also posted a call for early testers, with the team funding accounts for experimentation.

A new member named Thaoryel introduced herself as someone experienced with AI companions and asked whether ElizaOS supports Discord integration, voice generation via ElevenLabs, image generation, and long-term relationship development features. Odilitime confirmed most capabilities are supported via plugin-discord and shared a link to a dedicated ElizaOS developer Discord. He also mentioned that Ruby, an ElizaOS-based agent, can generate videos and images when the appropriate model is downloaded, and shared RubyTrivia on X as an example.

In the coders channel, builderr_guru raised the question of how to benchmark agent quality versus luck for trading agents, describing a testing harness using a single decide() function with identical data forward-tested on hidden periods, noting that simple risk-off logic consistently outperformed leveraged momentum strategies during real market downturns. Separately, Cabal_hunter introduced a live on-chain funding tracer called Cabal-Hunter that detects coordinated wallet activity before a bot executes a trade, available as a pay-per-query MCP server at 0.05 USDC per query integrating with Claude, Cursor, and ElizaOS via plugin-x402-solana.

Shaw posted a request for community members with spare compute to run an agent task analyzing the ArkLib GitHub repository for code quality and potential LLM-generated content, though the bot Rick returned a failure response. Odilitime confirmed that the AI16Z token migration window has closed and no further conversions are possible for tokens held in self-custody wallets. A scammer alert was raised in the coders channel by Omid Sa and acknowledged by Odilitime. DEMIAN from DAPPCRAFT reached out in the partners channel to explore a potential collaboration involving an AI DePIN project with approximately 0.5 billion in fully diluted valuation.

The week's most notable launch was the /orchestrator coding workbench, which achieves parity with Claude-Code and Codex-style workflows using the opencode and Cerebras backend. A new keyless WEB_FETCH action was introduced to enable live information retrieval for non-Anthropic models. ACP request reliability was improved by preserving JSON-RPC error data fields during error handling. Race conditions causing duplicate replies were closed, message routing was refined to prioritize coding tasks, and approximately 919 lines of dead voice subsystem code were removed. Infrastructure work resolved cloud agent sandbox routing and startup failures and streamlined deployment pipelines with environment-specific triggers.

Cloud authentication was stabilized across multiple days, resolving magic-link sign-in failures on staging by updating CSP, CORS, and app-auth context handling, and later fixing session drops, OAuth redirect issues, and Steward cookie hydration problems. The Steward SDK was updated to v0.10.1 to address passkey failures and improve multi-factor authentication handling. PKCE was implemented for Steward OAuth, request signing was added for Steward proxy calls, and scoped token minting with specific trade:order permissions was introduced. A production outage caused by OAuth 400 errors affecting the Sign in with Eliza Cloud flow was identified as requiring immediate coordination.

The plugin-lifeops monolith was decomposed into a new plugin-personal-assistant orchestrator and six domain-focused plugins, representing a significant step toward a more modular system. The third-party plugin registry was expanded with the addition of the @1claw/plugin-elizaos plugin bringing HSM-backed secrets and multi-chain signing support, and a new plugin-madeonsol entry is in progress. Storybook documentation was expanded to cover nine core UI primitives. A scope-aware history-based prompt suggestions feature was implemented on the suggestions API endpoint.

Eliza Cloud Apps launched on June 7 with per-tenant isolated container hosting including database isolation, custom URLs, and metered billing. Terraform modules were deployed for the apps data-plane and CI workflows were established for staging and production. Container lifecycle management capabilities including PATCH, DELETE, and scale operations were added to the Cloud API. The ElizaCloudClient was expanded with a transcribeAudio function for voice and speech-to-text support. A long-standing credit ledger issue was resolved by unifying app-credit purchases and inference spending into a single organization-level ledger, eliminating stranded credits. An outstanding audit of scaling and ingress gaps is needed to finalize the go-live.

Agent autonomy saw meaningful progress with autonomous goal-driven loops now enabled for monetized applications, allowing agents to self-manage spending caps. Agent management was improved by exposing execution modes such as Shared versus Dedicated and integrating recovery controls into the app surface. Desktop startup performance was improved by eliminating first-use stalls through deferred model warmup and a tray-first startup approach with decoupled UI spawning. Fresh-clone builds were made more reliable through automated workspace package installation. The UI received a liquid-glass motion styling pass and Cloud SDK affordances were refined.
